item.title: Android adds Gemini‑AI‑powered enhanced protection to Google Messages
item.description:
Android adds Gemini‑AI‑powered enhanced protection to Google Messages

Android is introducing new scam defense features that aim to make it easier for users to evade mobile fraud, including bolstered protection in Google Messages and additional safeguarding tools.

🔍 Overview

  • Android is using AI to suss out scammers in Google Messages.
  • A new “enhanced protection” setting will roll out in the coming weeks and is opt‑in.

🧩 How it works

  • The enhanced protection mode taps into cloud‑based Gemini AI models to quickly evaluate a potential scammer’s intentions in conversations with an unrecognized sender.
  • “Scammers often disguise their true motives behind slow‑burn conversations,” Google said.
  • “This secure cloud analysis augments and extends our existing on‑device detection, allowing us to identify novel and sophisticated attacks, actively uncovering and stopping abusers who try to hide their tracks.”
  • User data is encrypted during this AI analysis and processed in a secure dedicated space that Google (and anyone else besides the user) can’t access.
  • The mode also uses on‑device Gemini Nano AI to inspect real‑time web signals in unfamiliar URLs before they are opened to determine if the links are malicious.

⚙️ New security features

Feature Description
Call‑forwarding block Blocks apps from enabling call forwarding and notifies the user when someone attempts to do so.
Screen‑share privacy Automatically conceals sensitive information while screen‑sharing in Chrome and Android WebView.
Enhanced protection Opt‑in mode that uses Gemini AI to assess intentions of unrecognized senders and scans URLs with Gemini Nano.

🌐 Expansion and rollout

  • The scam detection feature for chat notifications that Google introduced on Pixel phones last year is expanding to devices from Honor, Motorola, Oppo, OnePlus, Realme, Tecno, Vivo, Xiaomi, and more.
  • Google says it plans to bring it to “hundreds of millions of additional users later this year.”

#Android #AI #Security #ScamDetection

Source: Android is using AI to suss out scammers in Google Messages

item.title: Google allows users to launch personal AI apps through Play Store
item.description:
Google allows users to launch personal AI apps through Play Store

Google has announced a new feature in the US that allows users to launch personal, vibe-coded apps directly through the Google Play Store.

🧩 How it works

  • Apps are launched using a standard Google account.
  • The feature is separate from the public store catalog, keeping the apps secure and private.
  • Users will soon have the ability to share these apps with a select group of people.

⚙️ Key details

  • Google first introduced the ability to vibe-code personal Android apps in May.
  • If users wish to share their app with the world, they can transition to a professional developer account.
  • Professional accounts are subject to the same Trust & Safety reviews and quality standards as existing professional developers, according to Sam Bright, Google’s vice president and general manager of Google Play.

🚀 Availability

  • This feature is currently available in the US.

#GooglePlay #Android #AppDevelopment #TechNews

Source: Google makes it easier to launch your vibe-coded apps

item.title: Google pushes Android 17 developer preview with battery and privacy enhancements
item.description:
Google pushes Android 17 developer preview with battery and privacy enhancements

The Android ecosystem is busy this weekend as Google released a fresh update to the Android 17 developer preview, focusing on better battery life, background‑process control, and new privacy tweaks.

🔍 Overview

  • Android 17 developer preview arrives with a revamped battery settings menu.
  • Users can now see which background services consume the most power.
  • A new Private Space folder lets you hide specific apps from the app drawer without uninstalling them.
  • Notification snooze lets you silence alerts for one or two hours.

⚙️ Key Details

  • Battery Management
    • Revamped battery settings menu.
    • Visibility of power‑hungry background services.
  • App Privacy
    • Hide apps in the Private Space folder.
    • Google aims to help users find apps that behave badly.
  • Notification Control
    • Swipe a notification to the side for a snooze option.

📱 Additional Android Updates

  • Google Maps – Minor update adds the ability to save multiple custom routes as home‑screen shortcuts.
  • Google Photos – Refresh includes a faster search index for quicker object and person searches.
  • Security Patch – October security patch released for all supported Pixel devices, fixing three major flaws that could allow unauthorized media‑file access. Other manufacturers (OnePlus, Motorola) expected to roll it out by mid‑next week.

🚀 Availability

  • The Android 17 preview is now available for developers.
  • Google plans to open the beta to more devices soon.
  • Reminder: Back up your data before installing major system updates; keeping copies of photos and documents is always wise.

💡 Why It Matters

  • Improved battery visibility helps users extend device runtime.
  • Enhanced privacy controls give users more granular app management.
  • Faster search in Google Photos and custom route shortcuts in Maps streamline everyday tasks.
  • The October security patch addresses critical vulnerabilities, reinforcing device security across the ecosystem.

#android #android17 #mobileupdates #privacy #security

Source: Android Daily News: October 10, 2026 – Latest Updates and Releases - thetechpapa

item.title: Google's Gemini AI to Automate Personal Phone Calls with 'Call for Me' Expansion
item.description:
Google’s Gemini AI to Automate Personal Phone Calls with ‘Call for Me’ Expansion

Google may be expanding its “Call for Me” AI feature beyond business calls so you can use it to send messages to friends and family.

🔍 Overview

Android Authority reports a “Gemini Calling” introductory screen in an APK teardown. The screen shows example prompts such as:

Example Prompt Intended Action
Call Mom and tell her I will be 15 minutes late Deliver a quick voice message to a family member
Call John and ask if he is coming for dinner Deliver a quick voice message to a friend

These examples suggest the feature would allow users to dictate short, text‑message‑style calls.

🧩 How it Works

  • Users issue a spoken prompt to Gemini (e.g., “Call Mom and tell her I will be 15 minutes late”).
  • Gemini generates a brief spoken message based on the prompt.
  • The AI places a phone call and plays the generated message, reaching the recipient without the user having to speak.
  • Android Authority also found “granular permissions” for Gemini actions in individual apps, including phone‑call permissions, letting users control which apps can invoke the feature.

⚙️ Key Details

  • The rumored Android update would automate personal phone calls with Gemini AI.
  • Gemini Call for Me might tell your mom you’re running late, or deliver other short updates.
  • Even with this expansion, Gemini would likely be limited to basic, text‑message‑like calls; it is not expected to conduct full, back‑and‑forth conversations.
  • Users could opt out of receiving incoming automated calls from Gemini via the granular permission settings.
  • Android Authority notes Google might choose not to publicly release the expansion or the permission controls.

🚀 Availability

  • The feature is currently rumored and has been observed in an APK teardown; no official release date or public announcement has been confirmed.

💡 Why it Matters

  • It offers a quick way to reach people who prefer phone calls, miss text messages, or still use landline phones.
  • The granular permission model could give users fine‑grained control over AI‑driven calling capabilities on Android devices.
  • If released, the feature would extend Google’s AI services from business contexts into everyday personal communication.

#Google #Gemini #AI #Android #CallForMe

Source: Gemini Call for Me might tell your mom you’re running late

item.title: Introduction of Docker-Android for Android Development and Testing
item.description:
Introduction of Docker-Android for Android Development and Testing

Docker-Android is a docker image designed to support all aspects of Android development and testing, including native, web, and hybrid-app projects.

⚙️ Key details

Docker-Android provides the following capabilities:

  • Ability to build Android projects.
  • Execution of unit and UI-Tests using frameworks such as Espresso and Appium.
  • VNC support to view the inside of the docker container.
  • Log sharing feature via a web-UI.
  • External control of the emulator using adb connect.
  • Integration with cloud solutions, including Genymotion Cloud.
  • Support for mcp server (beta-version).

🚀 Availability

Various image tags are available:

  • budtmo/docker-android:emulator_9.0
  • budtmo/docker-android:emulator_10.0
  • budtmo/docker-android:emulator_11.0
  • budtmo/docker-android:emulator_12.0
  • budtmo/docker-android:emulator_13.0
  • budtmo/docker-android:emulator_14.0
  • budtmo/docker-android:genymotion
  • budtmo/docker-android:mcp

📱 Device Profiles

The emulator supports various device profiles and skins:
